findings.finding: ‘We partly replicated the planning findings of Kupzyk (2011)’ gives an immediate aggregate verdict. The rest of the first sentence names the main source findings, followed by replay scope and numerical results.

findings.location: Section 1, opening paragraph continuing onto p. 2
findings.finding: ‘We partly replicated Kupzyk’s headline findings’ opens the section. The paragraph then specifies the reconstructed samples, unavailable replay inputs, paired contrasts, ICC pattern, and thresholds before explaining the general design.

The introduction defines the three kinds of power and the results give concrete comparisons and explanations in manuscript prose. The short ‘Disagreement record’ identifiers accompany rather than substitute for explanations.
The appendix explains the two regeneration routes in prose and commands.
The finite same-outcome comparison separates a refitting contribution from shrinking simulation error and leaves general equivalence unresolved.
Numerical agreement at the printed precision is a separate column from scope, and the prose separates rounding from Monte Carlo and mask comparisons.

The final exemplary grid recovers all five loss directions, the allocation-first ordering and the ICC .05 peak. The 8 versus 7 maximum and three one-cluster differences make the threshold component partial. Both sign counts exceed half (41 versus 40 of 54). The two partial component results support the aggregate opening verdict.

The 54/54 adjusted empirical comparisons and the extreme-setting Optimal Design departure agree with power-cell-comparison.csv and appendix-d-comparison.csv. They supplement the planning headline and do not replace it.

The hypothesis that attrition would dominate is distinguished from the empirical ordering in the dissertation. The ICC prose claim of a continuing decline is separately qualified by the source and rerun skewed-size increase; thresholds agree in 51 of 54 cells.

The three-method planning question (ch1), four research questions (rq1–rq4), predicted attrition ordering, 54 threshold comparisons and practical planning conclusion are present. The final-grid matched contrasts preserve all five losses and the illustrative reversal is explicitly a single pair.

The oversample item covers all six Table 3 rows, the tail cell, both observation-loss rounding variants, and the ch5 completers example. The contribution statement identifies the reported design and independent reconstruction.

ch3, appendix-a and appendix-b map to crossed settings, design factors, generator/REML checks and covariance checks. The formula-od and formula-bw findings give their distinct degrees of freedom and thresholds. The initial-empirical claim accounts for all 54 cells and both unadjusted outliers.

The initial-exemplary and final-exemplary items retain the 51 readable and 54 final comparison counts and 18 deterministic matches. The empirical-gap and baseline-50000 results retain both sign counts, the deficit and the same-outcome covariance diagnostic. All 324 Appendix C comparisons and the baseline Appendix D rates are described.

The null-baseline and null-extreme items retain distinct nominal, Bradley and Serlin assessments and the effective-df sensitivity. The Chapter II software examples and independent Figure 4 precision illustration retain both successful and unresolved results.

The regeneration and evidence table supports the aggregate Chapter IV (ch4) and discussion (ch5) claims and their components. Compared all 26 claim-map entries against the rendered locations and packet. The maps identify a starting page where paragraphs continue.
The practical ordering is scoped to the four-occasion Gaussian settings and specific dropout process.
The .88187 published cell is below the central rerun mask interval, and the feasible extreme mask is a diagnostic. The available-observation analysis explicitly excludes listwise deletion.
The paired effect is finite and restricted to the balanced baseline. General convergence or equivalence remains unresolved.

A smaller effective denominator can explain both Appendix D.2 rates, with original fitted state and degrees of freedom unresolved. Figure 4 seeds and the exact software input or convention behind the Optimal Design screens are unavailable.

The observed-count denominator extension is an assumption. Independent mask averages differ in estimand from the source realized designs. Rerun MCSE is a proxy for unobserved Appendix C source MCSE. Three hidden exemplary markers are excluded from figure-based comparisons while the separately reported full-grid count is retained.

Original fitted SAS records, random states, and realized masks are unavailable. Source PDF acquisition is separated from original-software availability. All ten packet limitations have an explicit rendered location.

Kupzyk (2011) is the Kevin A. Kupzyk dissertation identified on source physical PDF pp. 1–2 and linked as record 106 in the replication bibliography. Source PDF p. 4 supports the ordering and low-ICC moderation. Printed p. 97/Table 5 supports the maximum and pp. 106–107 the empirical/exemplary comparison.

The replay limitation is distinct from the new analysis. The reported and rerun mean losses, threshold maximum, and majority counts are in source-versus-ours order and agree with their independent inputs.

findings.location: Table 1, first five rows and note
findings.finding: Independently recomputed the signed losses from source Table 1 and rerun final-grid exemplary powers using matched reference-minus-violation pairs. The rendered pairs 1.327/1.275, 4.391/4.472, 6.409/6.443, .454/.438 and .851/.778 yield smaller/larger/larger/smaller/smaller with common positive direction. The two five-decimal power inputs contribute .0005 pp each to the .001 pp contrast bound.
The difference of 15% dropout losses at .05 minus .15 is 3.037/3.062 pp. The two contrast rounding bounds add to .002 pp. The rerun point estimate is larger and both signed effects are positive.

findings.location: Table 1, cluster and count rows and note
findings.finding: Maximum extra counts relative to the between–within reference are 8/7, and counts below exemplary minus half of 54 are 14/13. Both pairs are smaller and same direction using the .5-count printed-unit rule. Subtracting the exact majority reference adds no precision error.

The note explicitly separates the point-estimate magnitude labels from equivalence and scientific-pattern verdicts. Pages 3–7 explain the mask, reading, and Monte Carlo uncertainty underlying the different comparisons.

findings.location: Table 1, 5% dropout Published and Ours cells
findings.finding: The 1.3 pp Published result is stated on source p. 93 and matches Table 1/2 arithmetic. The 1.27 pp Ours result is the rounded 1.274814 pp final-grid paired mean.

findings.location: Table 1, 15% dropout Published and Ours cells
findings.finding: The 4.4 pp Published result is stated on source p. 93. The 4.47 pp Ours result is the rounded 4.471858 pp final-grid paired mean.

findings.location: Table 1, 70/30 allocation Published and Ours cells
findings.finding: The 6.4 pp Published result is stated on source p. 95 and backed by 27 Table 1 matched pairs. The 6.44 pp Ours result is the rounded 6.443263 pp mean over the corresponding final-grid pairs.

findings.location: Table 1, normal sizes Published and Ours cells
findings.finding: The .45 pp Published result is stated on source p. 95. The .44 pp Ours result is the rounded .438215 pp mean over the 18 matched rerun pairs.

findings.location: Table 1, skewed sizes Published and Ours cells
findings.finding: The .85 pp Published result is stated on source p. 95, with the sentence continued on p. 96. The .78 pp Ours result is the rounded .778279 pp matched rerun mean.

findings.location: Table 1, ICC Published and Ours cells
findings.finding: Source p. 96 reports the .05 peak and a subsequent decline in prose; Table 1 gives the counterexample .6098 to .6673 pp for skewed sizes from .10 to .15. The rerun counterpart has the .05 peak throughout and .5614 to .6248 pp on those skewed cells. Both cells distinguish the categorical finding from the separate scalar 15% dropout effect.

findings.location: Table 1, maximum extra clusters Published and Ours cells
findings.finding: Source Table 5 and accompanying text give 8 extra against the between–within references. The largest rerun excess over the same references is 7, and §2.1 supplies the condition-specific departures.

findings.location: Table 1, count below Published and Ours cells
findings.finding: The Published 41/54 is directly reported on source p. 106, independent of the three occluded markers. The Ours 40/54 is the count of negative rerun empirical-minus-exemplary cell differences.
